self_check.radical_uncertainty: Can't see actual relational dynamics—no user testimonials, interaction feel, team wellbeing, or how deliberations build (or erode) trust. Just a list of project names.
self_check.many_ways_of_knowing: Political lens would map power shifts in govt decisions; experimental on method iteration; epistemic on knowledge co-creation. I'd miss formal power analysis.
self_check.speed_of_wisdom: No premature warmth—content too thin, feels transactional on first read.
self_check.bigger_picture: Civic tech space: participatory platforms amid declining trust in institutions, competing with Polis, Decidim. Sits in govt-consultation ecology.
self_check.all_scales: Micro: individual idea submission; macro: govt/community decisions. Missing team/community relational health.
self_check.inner_work: Skeptical of tech mediation; might undervalue if it enables real talk, but evidence absent.

systemic.spectrum_position: symptom-treatment (tool for input into existing govt processes, not restructuring relational power)
systemic.evidence: evidence (platform aids 'better decisions' since 2008 via deliberation; lists govt/community consultations—no systemic critique)
systemic.reflective_question: Would persist as needed layer; doesn't dissolve relational govt-citizen divides.
systemic.watchout: Online platform likely simulates deliberation (votes/ideas) without embodied community ties.

experimentation.spectrum_position: fixed execution (mature platform, thousands of projects; diverse uses but no sign of hypothesis-testing)
experimentation.evidence: evidence (longevity since 2008, test communities suggest deployment over exploration)
experimentation.reflective_question: Unclear—scale implies feedback loops, but no info on model adaptation; probably wouldn't pivot core.
experimentation.watchout: Community lists as 'success metrics' without updating evidence.

fractality.spectrum_position: serves many scales lightly (global list: schools, govts, tests; extracts ideas broadly)
fractality.evidence: both (hundreds of shallow project names; no deep nourishment stories)
fractality.reflective_question: For participants, maybe empowering input; but thin info—likely not worth it purely internally without wider impact.
fractality.watchout: Broad reach over depth; extracts unpaid relational labor (deliberation) for govts.

non_identification.spectrum_position: tightly held (OntoStory GmbH platform; communities as users, not owners)
non_identification.evidence: evidence (corporate entity, hosted projects; no community fork/ownership hints)
non_identification.reflective_question: Unlikely—proprietary tool; wouldn't let communities redefine it.
non_identification.watchout: Rhetorical 'community' names mask platform control.

relational.felt_sense: Instrumental: funnels relational energy (ideas, debate) into data for decisions; useful but extractive, no warmth or depth visible.
relational.key_read: Scales relationally thin—treats community ties as input pipelines, not nourished fabric; political/experimental agents miss this emotional/labor extraction.

self_check.radical_uncertainty: High uncertainty due to extremely thin content—just a list of project names and a brief tagline. My read is tentative, heavily caveated by lack of substance.
self_check.many_ways_of_knowing: Political lens: Tool for governments to channel citizen input, potentially reinforcing top-down power via 'participation theater'. Relational: Enables deliberation in communities but as a hosted platform, relationships are mediated/technical.
self_check.speed_of_wisdom: Not blindly pattern-matching; this fits 'civic tech consultation platform' archetype (e.g., Pol.is, Consul), but content too sparse for confident epistemics read.
self_check.bigger_picture: Likely constrained by government clients—success means scaling consultations, failure means irrelevance; funding from donors/EU grants common in this space, biasing toward replication over disruption.
self_check.all_scales: Platform accrues learning institutionally (thousands of projects), but individual communities get one-off tools; no evidence of cross-learning.
self_check.inner_work: Slight bias toward projects with explicit humility/experiment docs; rewarding my preference for visible feedback loops over operational scale.

systemic.spectrum_position: Symptom-treatment (left): Platform aids isolated consultations without evident systemic power shifts.
systemic.evidence: intuition (thin list of govt/community projects; tagline on 'better decisions' but no structural analysis)
systemic.reflective_question: Success means more consultations, but systemic decision flaws (e.g., power imbalances) persist, making it permanently necessary.
systemic.watchout: Pure legibility: maps citizen prefs for govt use without challenging authority.

experimentation.spectrum_position: Fixed execution (left): Mature platform (2008, thousands of projects) implies replicated deployment, no visible hypothesis-testing.
experimentation.evidence: intuition (no mention of feedback loops, pivots, or metrics beyond project count)
experimentation.reflective_question: Unclear—content lacks any signal of monitoring core assumptions (e.g., does deliberation improve outcomes?); likely wouldn't notice quickly as it's scaled rigidly.
experimentation.watchout: Iteration theatre possible (many 'test' projects listed), but no evidence of real adaptation.

fractality.spectrum_position: Serves many scales lightly (rightish): Platform reused across global projects, but depth per community unknown.
fractality.evidence: both (project list shows broad use; tagline implies capacity-building via deliberation tools)
fractality.reflective_question: Marginally—for participants, it's a structured deliberation space, potentially valuable even if platform fails long-term.
fractality.watchout: Knowledge likely accrues to platform owners (OntoStory GmbH) via data, not communities.

non_identification.spectrum_position: Tightly held (left): Fixed platform for deliberation, mission-locked since 2008.
non_identification.evidence: intuition (longevity and scale suggest commitment to core model; no pivot stories)
non_identification.reflective_question: Doubtful—commercial entity (GmbH) with govt clients unlikely to abandon for radical change.
non_identification.watchout: Mission lock as 'proven' success (thousands of projects disguises potential unfalsifiability).

experimental.felt_sense: Operational civic tech tool, scaled but epistemically inert—feels like a black box for consultations without visible learning or humility; gut says 'works as intended but not innovative'.
experimental.key_read: No epistemic signals at all—pure deployment list lacks any trace of feedback, falsifiability, or updating; political/relational agents might praise participation scale, but this hides dogmatic replication.
